answer: CheXNet achieved an F1 score of 0.435 (95% CI 0.387, 0.481), which was higher than the radiologist average of 0.387 (95% CI 0.330, 0.442); the difference of 0.051 (95% CI 0.005, 0.084) did not include zero, so the authors concluded CheXNet's performance was statistically significantly higher than radiologist performance [1][3]. Med-PaLM 2 was compared with human experts in pairwise evaluations of long-form answers: physicians preferred Med-PaLM 2 answers to physician answers on eight of nine axes pertaining to clinical utility (p < 0.001), and Med-PaLM 2 answers were judged to better reflect medical consensus 72.9% of the time compared to physician answers; additionally, 90.6% of Med-PaLM 2 answers were rated as having low risk of harm, compared to 79.4% for Med-PaLM [6]. reference_answer: CheXNet reached an F1 score of 0.435 against a radiologist average of 0.387, exceeding the average radiologist on pneumonia detection.
